newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Nemtsov appointment leaves shares limp.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Nemtsov appointment leaves shares limp.

text.p: The appointment of Russia's favourite son Boris Nemtsov as Fuel and Energy Minister on Thursday failed to rouse a sluggish market, and traders said shares would likely stay range-bound into next week.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 shares closed slightly higher at 290.66 on light total market turnover of $22.3 million. The index closed at 290.22 on Wednesday.
"There's just so many announcements around, you kind of get numb to the news," said Renaissance Capital trader Victor Pitaleff.
Other dealers said the market had expected Nemtsov, who is also First Deputy Prime Minister, to be named as the head of the Fuel and Energy Ministry.
They said Western investors were buying, and that some stocks traded more actively, fuelled by individual announcements of 1996 profits and other news.
National power company Unified Energy System (UES) EESR.RTS announced 1996 net profit of 469 billion roubles, up from 442 billion roubles in 1995.

Trade in RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema (UES) shares picked up on the announcement, pushing values higher. But the stock soon retreated, closing slightly off at $0.2105 after $0.2109 on Wednesday.

Aton head trader Bobby Meshoyrer said a rise in household energy prices announced by regional energy company Mosenergo MSNG.RTS had a more noticeable impact on the firm's share price. Mosenergo rose to $1.235 from $1.229.
Despite the day's low trading volume, some traders said they expected the market to remain steady on Friday.
"A lot of investors are in town this week, catching up before the holidays," said Aton's Meshoyrer. "I see a lot of interest in the market to buy so I don't think it will go down."
He said investors were looking more at second and third tier shares.
"Telecoms and energy are still the favourites," he said.
But Pitaleff said he saw the market little changed in the short term.
"It was a very quiet day with not much activity in blue chips. I think we'll see more of the same for tomorrow," he said.
